{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Richard Allen Hunt''' (16 June 1937 &ndash; 22 March
2009) was an American [[mathematician]]. He graduated from [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1965 with a dissertation entitled ''Operators acting on [[Lorentz Spaces]]''.  An important result of {{harvtxt|Hunt|1968}} states that the [[Fourier expansion]] of a function in ''L''<sup>''p''</sup>, 
''p''&nbsp;> 1, converges almost everywhere.  The case ''p=2'' is due to [[Lennart Carleson]], and for this reason the general result is called the [[Carleson-Hunt theorem]].  Hunt was the 1969 recipient of the [[Salem Prize]]. He was a faculty member at [[Purdue University]] from 1969 to 2000, when he retired as professor emeritus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Obituary for Richard Hunt|date=March 24, 2009|website=Department of Mathematics, Purdue University|url=https://www.math.purdue.edu/news/2009/obituary-for-richard-hunt.html}}</ref>
